knowledge:
- key_parameters: gmt=A GeneSetCollection object containing the gene sets for functional annotation ;; reducedDimNames=The name of the reduced dimension slot in the SingleCellExperiment object containing the 2D coordinates (e.g., "PCA") ;; assayNames=The name of the assay slot in the SingleCellExperiment object containing the gene expression data (e.g., "normcounts") ;; ndim=The number of dimensions (latent variables) to estimate in calcTGIF ;; html.open=Logical value in reportTGIF indicating whether to automatically open the generated HTML report in a browser
- alternatives: Known marker gene expression (requires expert knowledge, not general-purpose) ;; BLAST-like gene expression comparison with reference DB (limited if cell type is unknown or unmeasured) ;; Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) and over-representation analysis (ORA) (ambiguous, time-consuming, and dependent on cluster labels)
- when_to_use: Use when analyzing unannotated single-cell RNA-Seq data to directly link spatial/2D-coordinate cell patterns to functional gene sets without relying on prior clustering or marker gene lists.
- pitfalls: Only NCBI Gene IDs (Entrez IDs) are supported for gene identifiers ;; Using raw counts instead of normalized gene expression is supported but normalized data (e.g., registered in normcounts) is highly recommended ;; The reportTGIF function can take some time to run ;; The category argument of msigdbr() is deprecated (use collection instead)

workflows.name: sctgif_analysis
workflows.intent: Perform joint NMF on single-cell RNA-Seq data and gene sets to generate attention maps and functional annotations, followed by an HTML report.
input: DistalLungEpithelium (gene expression matrix with Entrez IDs)
workflows.stages: 1. Load and prepare the gene set collection ;; 2. Create a SingleCellExperiment object with the expression matrix and 2D coordinates ;; 3. Normalize the expression data and register it in the normcounts slot ;; 4. Initialize parameters using settingTGIF ;; 5. Perform joint NMF using calcTGIF ;; 6. Generate an HTML report using reportTGIF
workflows.code:
library("scTGIF")
library("SingleCellExperiment")
library("GSEABase")
library("msigdbr")

data("DistalLungEpithelium")
data("pca.DistalLungEpithelium")
data("label.DistalLungEpithelium")

m_df = msigdbr(species = "Mus musculus",
    category = "H")[, c("gs_name", "entrez_gene")]

hallmark = unique(m_df$gs_name)
gsc <- lapply(hallmark, function(h){
    target = which(m_df$gs_name == h)
    geneIds = unique(as.character(m_df$entrez_gene[target]))
    GeneSet(setName=h, geneIds)
})
gmt = GeneSetCollection(gsc)
gmt = gmt[1:10] # Reduced for this demo

sce <- SingleCellExperiment(assays = list(counts = DistalLungEpithelium))
reducedDims(sce) <- SimpleList(PCA=pca.DistalLungEpithelium)

CPMED <- function(input){
    libsize <- colSums(input)
    median(libsize) * t(t(input) / libsize)
}
normcounts(sce) <- log10(CPMED(counts(sce)) + 1)

settingTGIF(sce, gmt, reducedDimNames="PCA", assayNames="normcounts")

calcTGIF(sce, ndim=3)

reportTGIF(sce,
    html.open=FALSE,
    title="scTGIF Report for DistalLungEpithelium dataset",
    author="Koki Tsuyuzaki")
